Because the probability of obtaining this result was not lower than the significance level,
we did not reject the null hypothesis. That means that we did not have conclusive evidence that the
proportion of Americans who believe marijuana should be legal for medical and recreational use
What is the potential error we could be making with this conclusion? It is possible that the null
hypothesis (that the population proportion is equal to 60%) is wrong, but we did not reject it.

This section contains the outline of hypothesis testing. The language can certainly be confusing, and you
are not alone if you find it complicated. The next two sections will detail how the process works for
hypotheses about population proportions for qualitative variables (section 8.2) and hypotheses about
population means of quantitative variables (section 8.3). Section 8.4 will summarize and differentiate
between the tests. For the remainder of the chapter, we will be following the steps shown in the
reproduced below. Hopefully, it will help to make the process clearer.
